Configure your server

Models

Choose the deployment’s default model, connect local or OpenAI-compatible servers, and configure approvals, media generation and voice.

English | 简体中文

Deployment model

The deployment model is used by anyone who has not connected a model of their own. PI_DEFAULT_PROVIDER picks the provider and PI_DEFAULT_MODEL the model:

PI_DEFAULT_PROVIDER Key Default model
openrouter (default) OPENROUTER_API_KEY anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5
anthropic ANTHROPIC_API_KEY claude-sonnet-5
deepseek DEEPSEEK_API_KEY deepseek-flash

Pick a vision-capable model so screenshot computer tools stay available.

A provider that authenticates from the host needs no key: for Amazon Bedrock with an ECS task, IRSA or EC2 instance role, opt in with PI_DEFAULT_CREDENTIALS=host and set PI_DEFAULT_PROVIDER=amazon-bedrock, PI_DEFAULT_MODEL and AWS_REGION. With an instance role, keep restricted computer egress on so bot computers cannot read the role’s credentials from the metadata endpoint.

Google Vertex works the same way with PI_DEFAULT_PROVIDER=google-vertex, using the host’s application default credentials (GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT, GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION). Runs on host credentials are billed to that cloud account.

The Compose files also pass the standard provider key variables the agent runtime reads itself (OPENAI_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY, MISTRAL_API_KEY, GROQ_API_KEY, XAI_API_KEY and others) to the API and worker, for models that have no stored credential.

RAKAZO_LIVE_MODEL_CATALOG=off disables provider and Codex live catalog probing; the default is on.

Approvals

Approvals have three modes in Settings → Approvals: Never ask skips ordinary approval prompts, Auto lets an approval model pass actions that fit the request, and Ask asks before any change. A space starts in Auto, which asks like Ask until an approval model is available. Each person can allow or block single tools and sites in every mode, and a space can customize its approvals apart from the account. All modes still enforce block rules and safety checks. Purchases always require a person’s approval; unattended runs that cannot request approval refuse them.

In Settings → Models → Approval model, each user can select a model from an existing connection and add ordered backups, independently of their main model. Personal connections use their own credentials; hosted calls follow the same WhatEverFi credit rules as chat. Backups are tried only when a checker fails. An explicit ask, including an uncertain decision, still requires a person.

The deployment checker remains the default when no approval model is selected. For OpenRouter Jev, set RAKAZO_AUTO_REVIEW_PROVIDER=openrouter and RAKAZO_AUTO_REVIEW_MODEL=typesafe/jev-1.14; it uses OPENROUTER_API_KEY and the Decisions API. TypeSafe direct remains available through RAKAZO_AUTO_REVIEW_PROVIDER=jev and TYPESAFE_API_KEY. Core runs without either hosted service.

With TypeSafe, RAKAZO_AUTO_REVIEW_MODEL defaults to jev-latest, and RAKAZO_AUTO_REVIEW_MIN_CONFIDENCE (0 to 1, default 0.5) is the confidence below which Auto asks the person instead. RAKAZO_AUTO_REVIEW_TIMEOUT_MS (200 to 30000, default 10000) bounds each check.

Local models

To use an operator-controlled OpenAI-compatible server such as Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, or MLX, list its model IDs and an endpoint that both the API and worker processes can reach:

RAKAZO_LOCAL_MODELS=qwen3:4b,llama3.1:8b,qwen3-vl
RAKAZO_LOCAL_MODELS_URL=http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1
# Optional: key for a server that requires one, sent as the bearer token.
RAKAZO_LOCAL_MODELS_API_KEY=
RAKAZO_LOCAL_CONTEXT_WINDOW=32768
RAKAZO_LOCAL_MAX_TOKENS=4096
# Optional: model ids on this endpoint that accept images (screenshot computer tools).
RAKAZO_LOCAL_VISION_MODELS=qwen3-vl
# Optional: model ids on this endpoint that accept OpenAI-style reasoning_effort.
RAKAZO_LOCAL_REASONING_MODELS=qwen3:4b

Set RAKAZO_LOCAL_MODELS_API_KEY when the server requires a key, such as LiteLLM, vLLM started with --api-key, or a company gateway. Every request to RAKAZO_LOCAL_MODELS_URL then sends it as Authorization: Bearer; unset, requests carry the placeholder local. Like the other deployment keys, it stays on the API and worker and is redacted from run output. Use HTTPS unless the network is trusted. To make a local model the deployment model, set PI_DEFAULT_PROVIDER=local, PI_DEFAULT_MODEL to one of RAKAZO_LOCAL_MODELS and PI_DEFAULT_CREDENTIALS=host.

A model in RAKAZO_LOCAL_REASONING_MODELS offers thinking levels and sends the chosen level as reasoning_effort (medium by default, none when thinking is off). Other local models never receive the field.

RAKAZO_LOCAL_MAX_TOKENS is the output limit sent with every request to a local model, unless the connection sets its own max-tokens value. It never exceeds a quarter of RAKAZO_LOCAL_CONTEXT_WINDOW, so the prompt keeps the rest; a higher limit leaves less room for the prompt, so long chats are compacted sooner.

The loopback default is suitable when running WhatEverFi from a source checkout. From containers, prefer a stable LAN RFC1918 address (not Compose service DNS alone). On Docker Desktop, host.docker.internal also works. On Docker Desktop, a bot computer shell can often reach services bound to host 127.0.0.1 through that same hostname. Do not run sensitive unauthenticated services on loopback while bots run, or firewall / block that path. Linux does not get host.docker.internal the same way by default. Only configure an endpoint you control: prompts, attachments, and tool results sent to that model leave WhatEverFi through this URL. Leave RAKAZO_LOCAL_MODELS blank to disable the provider.

Ollama Cloud

In Settings → Models, choose Ollama Cloud, paste an API key from ollama.com, then Find models. This uses an OpenAI-compatible connection with no environment configuration, and stays available when RAKAZO_OPENAI_COMPAT_ALLOW_PUBLIC=0.

OpenAI-compatible connections

Each user can also connect their own OpenAI-compatible endpoint from Connect a model / Settings → Models on web and mobile. Choose OpenAI-compatible, enter the server base URL (for example http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1), the exact model id, and an optional API key. Add optional request headers under Advanced; values are stored encrypted, and only their names are shown afterwards. Public hosts and ordinary hostnames need HTTPS when they receive an API key or custom headers, and must resolve only to public addresses. Set RAKAZO_OPENAI_COMPAT_ALLOW_PUBLIC=0 on the API and worker to block them. Literal private IP, loopback, and host.docker.internal targets do not, but they are refused unless MCP_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ENDPOINT=true is set on the API and worker, which allows them for every user. This is checked on save, on model discovery, and on every run. With the Docker images install and the desktop app, a localhost or 127.0.0.1 connection reaches the computer running Docker (through host.docker.internal). On Linux, the model server must listen on an address the Docker bridge can reach, not only 127.0.0.1. For a self-hosted endpoint whose hostname resolves to private IPs, set RAKAZO_OPENAI_COMPAT_PRIVATE_HOSTS=models.example.test,other.example.test in the deployment environment for both API and worker, then recreate those containers. Entries are exact hostnames (case-insensitive, optional trailing dot), not URLs, suffixes, or wildcards. These hosts ignore RAKAZO_OPENAI_COMPAT_ALLOW_PUBLIC; every DNS answer must be private, and metadata and link-local destinations remain blocked. This applies to discovery and model requests. HTTPS still validates the hostname’s certificate. Like private IP endpoints, trusted hostnames also permit HTTP with API keys; use HTTPS unless the network is trusted. Only allow hosts you control. Private endpoints require MCP_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ENDPOINT=true for the deployment; no app account bypasses that policy. If that endpoint’s model accepts images, enable Supports images under Advanced when connecting so attachments and screenshot computer tools stay available. Existing connections default to disabled. For centrally managed endpoints, the deployment-wide fallback remains RAKAZO_OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_VISION_MODELS=gpt4o-vision,llava.

Thinking

For servers that accept standard reasoning_effort, enable Supports thinking under Advanced when connecting. The setting is saved on the connection (no env var or restart). Existing connections default to disabled. Deployment-local models opt in through RAKAZO_LOCAL_REASONING_MODELS; reconnect through Settings → Models only to move to a personal connection.

Enabled connections default to medium thinking. Web and desktop expose Thinking in a bot’s advanced settings; mobile inherits the same backend policy. WhatEverFi sends standard reasoning_effort (minimal, low, medium, high, or none when off); the server owns model-specific translation. Leave Supports thinking off when the server lacks standard effort support. Existing token limits still apply; effort is not a separate reasoning-token budget.

Prompt cache capabilities

The model connection API accepts cacheCapabilities, including scope, retentionMs, minimumTokens, and retentionMode. Declare a positive retentionMs only when the endpoint supports prefix reuse for that window. For these connections with usable history-retrieval tools, the runtime automatically uses cache-aware context: recent history remains bounded on a cold request, and subsequent requests keep that selected prefix while it is likely warm and fits the context budget. Connections with unknown retention or retentionMode: "none" retain the default retrieval policy. An explicit executor context strategy still takes precedence. Callers without usable history-retrieval tools keep fitting original history under the model’s context budget instead of replacing it with snapshots.

Cache warmth is advisory. Changing instructions or tools, context pressure, worker eviction, or a process restart can require fresh prompt processing. These settings do not create backend KV snapshots or keep a model loaded; the inference server is responsible for retention and conversation switching.

Paid data services

Bots can look up paid data (map places, search results, work emails, people and company profiles, social posts, SEO data) through one deployment account. It is off by default. Configure the worker (and API for inline execution):

PAID_SERVICES_PROVIDER=treg
PAID_SERVICES_API_KEY=replace-with-org-scoped-token

PAID_SERVICES_PROVIDER accepts disabled (the default), treg, or fake (for offline testing only). PAID_SERVICES_BASE_URL points at a self-hosted Treg instead of https://treg.to. Use an org-scoped token, and keep the account topped up or on automatic top-up: an empty balance makes every call fail.

Bots get service_search and service_call in every run; service_call follows the bot’s approval mode like other actions. Only read-only lookups are offered: actions on accounts, generation tasks, and services that need the account’s own connections are left out. Each call has a cost ceiling the bot sets and the approval card shows (at most $2) that the provider enforces before it charges. When model credits are on, a call first holds that ceiling from the organization’s credits and then settles to what the provider charged plus 20%, never above the ceiling; calls the provider does not bill are free. A call that may have run without an answer keeps its hold for the credit reconciler to flag. Every call appears in Usage under the services provider.

Image and video generation

Bot media tools are disabled by default. Configure the worker (and API for inline execution) with a provider and its generic HTTP connection:

MEDIA_GENERATION_PROVIDER=fal
MEDIA_GENERATION_BASE_URL=https://queue.fal.run
MEDIA_GENERATION_API_KEY=replace-with-media-api-key
MEDIA_GENERATION_IMAGE_MODEL=fal-ai/flux/schnell
MEDIA_GENERATION_VIDEO_MODEL=fal-ai/wan/v2.2-a14b/text-to-video

MEDIA_GENERATION_PROVIDER accepts disabled (the default), fal, or fake (for offline testing only). The base URL is optional and defaults to the URL above. Only set the image/video model fields for capabilities you want enabled. Compatible servers can use the same connection fields; models must support the corresponding fal queue API and Flux/Wan input and output shapes. Credentials stay on the server. Set these in your deployment secret configuration; never commit actual credentials.

Bots use generate_image to attach one PNG or generate_video to submit a four-second MP4. The video tool returns a job ID and queued/running status. The worker keeps checking the job in the background, including after a restart, and posts the finished video to the chat that asked for it, once; the bot then gets a turn to follow up. A video that fails, or is still unfinished after an hour, is marked failed and the bot gets a turn to say so. The bot can also call the tool again with jobId to check progress. Use the existing per-bot tool switches and action approval rules to control access. Both tools require approval by default. Ticket board runs keep these chat-only media tools unavailable so ticket work stays on the board.

Each run allows at most two submissions (including failures). Submissions are never retried automatically: a lost response can mean the provider accepted and charged for the request. Provider errors omit remote response bodies. Configure account budgets and rate limits with your provider; the run cap is not a currency budget. Provider 429 responses are returned without automatic retries. Outputs must fit both the 10 MiB media ceiling and the configured attachment limit; larger outputs are rejected.

Images use existing inline chat rendering. MP4 files can be previewed with native video controls on web and Electron and opened/downloaded through the existing native file flow on mobile. No new mobile player or settings screen is required.

Voice

macOS voices

When the API runs on macOS, Voice settings also offers macOS, which needs no key. The API renders each reply with the built-in /usr/bin/say into an audio clip, so it plays on the listener’s device and stops like any other voice. Docker and Linux hosts do not list it.

Spoken summaries

Off by default. Set VOICE_SUMMARY_MIN_CHARS (for example 600) to have a voice read a bot reply longer than that many characters as a short summary written by that bot’s own model. Each summary is an extra model call billed to the bot. The chat keeps the full reply, and if the summary call fails the full reply is read.

Fish Audio

FISH_TTS_MODEL sets the Fish Audio speech model for connections that do not choose one (default s2.1-pro), and FISH_ASR_MODEL the transcription model (default transcribe-1-pro). Set them on the API and worker.

Calls

Bots can call a user in the app, and users can hold to talk, when PHONE_CALLS_ENABLED=true is set on the API and worker. PHONE_CALL_COOLDOWN_MINUTES (default 2) is the minimum time between a bot’s calls to the same person, and PHONE_CALL_RING_SECONDS (default 45) how long an unanswered call rings.

For native mobile ringing and optional APNs VoIP configuration, see Mobile incoming calls.
